The Reserve Bank reported little evidence yet of AI disrupting the labour market but flagged high uncertainty about future effects. Opposition figures criticised the approach as voluntary guidance while companies such as Qantas, National Australian Bank and Canva cut thousands of jobs linked partly to AI.
items.title: Australia warns employers of AI job and wage effects

items.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit a building housing Nasser Hospital's surgical and intensive care wards in southern Gaza, killing at least five Palestinians, including reportedly a surgeon. The Hamas-run Civil Defence agency reported the death toll of 20 people injured. Israel says it targeted militants using medical infrastructure as a command center.
items.title: Israeli Strike on Gaza Hospital Kills at Least Five

items.summary: A BBC report describes how Russia's intensified attacks on Ukraine's energy grid are pushing power supplies close to critical, leaving families in Kyiv facing outages of up to 20 hours. Daryna Kulchytska, a single parent, recounts unreliable rolling blackouts that have been in place since October and are lasting longer than last winter. The article shows the damage at one large power station destroyed by a ballistic missile strike, with recovery hampered by air raids every 15-30 minutes. President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine still has enough generating capacity but struggles to deliver it home; Maxim Timchenko of DTEK warns attacks have doubled in scale and rebuilding will take until next summer.
items.title: Ukraine's Power Grid Near Collapse as Russian Strikes Intensify

items.summary: Michael Lee from the Republic of Korea came to China in 2003, and more than two decades later he now calls Quanzhou in Fujian Province his home. In Jinjiang, a county-level city under Quanzhou and one of China's leading footwear manufacturing hubs, he found a world-class supply chain, constant innovation, and the opportunity to build his own business. His next big plan is to become a true local.
items.title: ROK Entrepreneur Roots His Business in China's Shoe Capital

items.summary: Hundreds of thousands took to the streets across Spain on Wednesday for its first general strike in 14 years, protesting a housing crisis and low wages. Estimates of turnout varied widely between organisers and authorities; Madrid police counted 120,000 against an organiser's half million claim (quantity-1210-1217). More than 70 people were arrested nationwide amid clashes with riot police (quantity-86-95), while unions reported high participation in ports and industry. Unions called it a success; employers dismissed it as a failure.
items.title: Spain's First General Strike in 14 Years Draws Mass Protests

items.summary: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng Svendsen alleged that the Indian embassy in Oslo stopped her from travelling to a Congress-organised summit in Hyderabad, cancelling her visa 10 minutes before she left for the airport. She said “orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa,” suggesting political motivation tied to her May questioning of Narendra Modi and criticism of Adani and Ambani. The home ministry, external affairs ministry and embassy had not commented. About 200 international delegates attended; clearance was obtained for 316 foreign delegates.
items.title: Norwegian Journalist Alleges India Cancelled Her Visa

items.summary: Premier David Crisafulli officially reopened the New Burton Coal Mine in Queensland's Bowen Basin, employing 275 workers after receivership in 2025. Owner Argo Resources Queensland said coal royalties did not deter investment and declined to comment on previous owners' losses. CEO Richard Livingstone-Blevins planned to mine 10 million tonnes by 2028.
items.title: Queensland Reopens Coal Mine After Royalty Concerns

items.summary: The Australian government cancelled its search for a National Solar Panel Recycling Pilot administrator on 10 November, citing undisclosed changes to the industry since April’s tender release. The pilot would have engaged a supplier to collect up to 250,000 decommissioned panels from around 100 sites and recycle them safely.
items.title: Australia Cancels Solar Panel Recycling Pilot

items.summary: Cupid reported September-quarter revenue from operations of Rs 188 crore, up 122% year-on-year, with net profit reaching Rs 56 crore against Rs 24 crore a year earlier. The company raised FY27-FY29 guidance for higher revenue and profitability. Shares rose about 577% over the past year, valuing at around Rs 48,407 crore market capitalisation.
items.title: Cupid Shares Rally on Strong Q2 Profit and Raised Guidance

items.summary: Ola Electric shares rose to Rs 37 apiece, noted as only the second time in a month the stock crossed this level. The sharp 9% surge over two days added more than Rs 1,400 crore to market capitalisation, pushing it above Rs 17,150 crore. The rise follows the Finance Ministry making EVs the default and preferred choice for government staff car procurement, doubling the net dealer price ceiling to Rs 20 lakh while ICE vehicles are fixed at Rs 10 lakh.
items.title: Ola Electric Shares Rise on EV Procurement Policy

items.summary: Zhao Jiyou of the Latin America Branch of China Railway No. 10 Engineering Co., Ltd. describes infrastructure projects across three countries as part of a CGTN series with SASAC on state-owned enterprises in Asia-Pacific connectivity. The group is reinforcing a roadbed in Piura, Peru's northwestern region; it completed rehabilitation of mountain roads at an altitude of 4,500 meters and built the Santiago Apóstol Hospital in Utcubamba with UNOPS support. In Chile, its earlier railway work earned EFE awards. Zhao Jiyou says building connectivity requires both physical infrastructure and closer people-to-people ties.
items.title: China Railway Group Details Peru and Chile Infrastructure Work

items.summary: The Union government reduced India's visa categories from 13 to 9 and sub-categories from 23 to 49, per the Ministry of Home Affairs (quantity-82-83, quantity-89-91, quantity-114-116). Application-form fields were cut by roughly two-thirds. The changes aim to ease travel for tourism, medical treatment, education and business, with visas expected by end of 2026.
items.title: India Cuts Visa Categories and Simplifies Application Forms

items.summary: On Thursday, Israeli occupiers attacked the West Bank town of Atara under army protection, assaulting residents and damaging vehicles while leaving several Palestinians injured, local sources said. Clashes prompted the army to enter the town and fire tear gas canisters, stun grenades and live ammunition. Around 750,000 settlers occupy settlements across the region.
items.title: Israeli forces attack Palestinian town of Atara

items.summary: Veeraswamy, the UK’s oldest Indian restaurant on London’s Regent Street and a venue that served Churchill, Chaplin and Brando, faces closure after The Crown Estate declined to renew its lease at Victory House for renovation work. Owner Ranjit Mathrani says the business is being treated unfairly; the landlord rejects this claim. The dispute now proceeds under the Landlord and Tenant Act, with court proceedings begun on November 5 determining whether Veeraswamy can keep its lease.
items.title: Veeraswamy restaurant forced to close as Crown Estate declines lease renewal

items.summary: Former Uttarakhand Chief Minister Harish Rawat said he will not seek the chief minister’s post or any other office if Congress wins a majority in the 2027 Assembly elections, according to Press Trust of India. His stated goal is helping Congress form the state government and ousting the BJP.
items.title: Harish Rawat Rules Out CM Bid

items.summary: This morning briefing summarizes several Thursday news items. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, per Russian media (s1). Kirill Dmitriev met them at Vnukovo Airport (s2). Israel's security cabinet ordered military preparations for a possible attack on Iran, reported by KAN (s6), which warned the directives could trigger war (s7); they followed Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot's statement urging Netanyahu to refrain from operations until after Oct. 27 elections (s8-s10). Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan emphasized leaving a cleaner world for future generations at COP31 in Türkiye (s12-s14). FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem said Formula One races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will proceed as scheduled despite Middle East tensions (s17).
items.title: Morning Briefing Covers Russia Talks and Global News

items.summary: A fire swept through Parsi Parlo town in Arunachal Pradesh’s Kurung Kumey district early Thursday morning, killing at least four people including three children and a woman. Police sources said the blaze broke out around 2am and was suspected to have originated in a kitchen, though its exact cause remains under investigation. The tragedy exposed the lack of firefighting infrastructure in the remote area.
items.title: Fire Kills Four in Arunachal’s Kurung Kumey

items.summary: An article argues that India is working to revive its Vishwaguru image through a limited role in the ongoing peace talks, which are being brokered by the US. New Delhi stays off the negotiation table but focuses on protecting Indian seafarers and maintaining grain supplies for the Global South. Kanwal Sibal says these reflect two immediate concerns: the welfare of Indian seafarers and commercial shipping safety. Ambassador Anil Wadhwa notes that India's shift toward concrete proposals reflects greater diplomatic confidence, though he warns against overstating its capacity to broker a final settlement.
items.title: India's Modest Role in Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks

items.summary: The Global wildlife trade regulator CITES has lifted sanctions imposed on Laos in 2023 for failing to control criminal networks trading illegal wildlife products. Laos will now be able to trade in CITES-listed animals without special restriction, but remains under ongoing monitoring. Some conservationists called the move “premature,” arguing that Laos must do more to curb the illegal wildlife trade, which is estimated to be worth billions of dollars a year globally. In 2025, a joint Mongabay investigation with NGO GI-TOC identified 35 illegal wildlife shopping sites in Vientiane and Luang Prabang selling ivory, rhino horn, pangolin scales and other products. By July 2026 the number had grown before most shops closed by August 2026. Authorities reportedly inspected 25 shops, ordered six to close and detained 27 foreign nationals.
items.title: CITES Lifts Sanctions on Laos Amid Conservation Concerns

items.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s opposition has condemned a new law enacted by President Félix Tshisekedi that opens the door to constitutional changes, accusing him of seeking to extend his power. Jean-Baptiste Kasekwa said Tshisekedi “openly declares that he wants to remain in power until someone strong enough can drive him out.” The opposition has vowed to resist any change and called for elections scheduled for 2028, though a researcher noted it is difficult to envision holding them given the security context. Former president Joseph Kabila’s armed movement threatens force against what they call tyranny.
items.title: DRC Opposition Vows Resistance to Tshisekedi Constitutional Changes

items.summary: Chief Minister V D Satheesan said ensuring quality fuel is non-negotiable and oil companies' interests cannot take priority over people's welfare. The government directed the Civil Supplies Department to intensify petrol pump inspections, with nine samples collected on November 9 from Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Kannur districts. Results are expected within ten days, and violations will invite legal action.
items.title: Kerala CM Prioritises Consumer Fuel Quality Over Oil Firms

items.summary: Kia India will invest USD 2 billion to build a new manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh, per Gwanggu Lee, Managing Director and CEO of Kia India. The project is expected to create around 12,000 jobs and raise annual production capacity to more than 6 lakh units.
items.title: Kia India Announces USD 2 Billion Investment in Andhra Pradesh

items.summary: Crude oil prices declined as traders weighed hopes for peace in Ukraine and Iran ahead of a US-China summit, with Brent at $91.32 per barrel and WTI at $85.32 (quantity-227-233, quantity-297-303). Reports of higher OPEC production and rising US inventories added downward pressure, though Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks limited losses.
items.title: Oil Prices Fall on Ukraine-Iran Peace Hopes
